name: Oak Ridge High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR)
notes: Beryllium-reflected flux-trap reactor delivering one of the highest steady-state neutron fluxes in the world (2.5e15 n/cm2-s). Produces Cf-252, Pu-238, Ac-225, and other key radioisotopes.

name: Advanced Test Reactor (ATR)
notes: Serpentine cloverleaf core geometry allows nine separate test loops at independent flux levels. Primary US test bed for naval propulsion and advanced reactor materials.

name: Chalk River Laboratories (NRU / Research)
notes: Historic heavy-water universal research reactor; supplied up to 40% of the world's medical isotopes (Mo-99) for decades. Site of Brockhouse's Nobel prize-winning neutron scattering.

name: OPAL Open Pool Australian Lightwater Reactor
notes: Open pool reactor with heavy water reflector tank. Major southern-hemisphere source of medical Mo-99, I-131, and neutron scattering facilities.

name: BR2 High-Flux Materials Testing Reactor
notes: Hyperbolic twisted beryllium matrix core allowing high-density irradiation channels. Critical European supplier of medical isotopes and fusion reactor materials testing.

name: HANARO Research Reactor
notes: Open-pool-type multi-purpose research reactor in Daejeon. Dedicated to neutron science, cold neutron beams, fuel qualification, and radioisotope production.

name: High Flux Reactor (HFR) Petten
notes: Tank-in-pool reactor producing medical radioisotopes for over 30,000 patient treatments per day across Europe.

name: FRM II Research Neutron Source Heinz Maier-Leibnitz
notes: Compact cylindrical core surrounded by heavy water moderator producing the highest thermal neutron flux per MWth in Europe.

name: Maria Research Reactor
notes: Pool reactor with pressurized channels and beryllium matrix. Major producer of I-131, Lu-177, and silicon doping for power electronics.

name: SAFARI-1 Research Reactor
notes: Tank-in-pool materials testing reactor in Pelindaba; pioneer in converting from HEU to LEU targets for commercial Mo-99 production.
